label: VERIFIED unless stated; see numbers in the sections above
hazard_1_flat_vector_scan_plus_IN_list: CONFIRMED. No ANN index; LanceDB flat scan with the all-READY-ids IN prefilter costs ~2.4 us/row p50 (1.14 s at 500k rows, 4.7 s at 2M, 9.7 s at 4M, 19.6 s at 8M rows); the IN filter adds ~60-70% over an unfiltered flat scan. 1 s crossed at ~436k chunks (~14.5k files at 30 chunks/file), 5 s at ~2.1M chunks (~71k files). With IVF_PQ (nprobes 20, refine 10) p50 is 0.1-0.5 s at 2M-8M rows (recall@30 0.83-1.0 on clustered synthetic data), but the IN prefilter itself still scales linearly with rows. SQLite eligible-id load and IN string build are negligible (<0.05 s at 67k versions).
hazard_2_sequential_ingest: CONFIRMED, and worse than predicted: per-file index-write cost grows with library size. On 3,495 docx/pptx files (90k chunks): FTS5 write per chunk rose ~11x (0.002 s -> ~0.022 s), existing-id checks ~13x, Lance write ~8x; end-to-end per-file wall rose from 0.62 s to ~1.3 s. Cause (code reading + timing): fts_chunks.chunk_id is an UNINDEXED FTS5 column so every DELETE-before-INSERT and every 'chunk_id IN (...)' existence check is a full scan; Lance merge_insert/existence checks scan chunk_id too. Total index cost is therefore quadratic in library size. Embedding itself ran at ~57-106 chunks/s end-to-end.
hazard_3_docling_and_page_images: CONFIRMED. Docling runs on CPU only here (torch cu130 build, cuda unavailable): 0.37 pages/s on CUAD contracts (264 pages in 707 s, scanned/OCR-heavy). Page PNG store: ~300 KB/page (79 MB for 264 pages from 1.9 MB of PDFs = 34x the raw PDF bytes).
hazard_4_triple_text_storage: CONFIRMED. Chunk text is stored in SQLite chunks, again in FTS5 (fts_chunks_content + fts_chunks_data), and in LanceDB; plus Lance manifests: with one fragment/version per file the _versions directory was 527 MB vs 426 MB of data for 3,495 files (manifest growth is superlinear).
hazard_5_no_scale_tests: n/a (the scripts in this directory are the first).
xlsx_heavy_file_observation: VERIFIED (aborted run): one generated 4.6 MB xlsx (~20k rows x 5 sheets) produced 70,180 chunks (15 chunks per KB, ~200 B/chunk); after 25+ min the file was still embedding (qwen3-embedding batch 32, sharing the GPU with another agent's eval) and was killed; 29 smaller files before it had finished. Spreadsheets therefore dominate chunk counts: ~15,000 chunks per MB for dense tabular xlsx.
